title: 2026 Season Power Rankings
subtitle: Pre-Week 5 board, post-waivers. Goats still alone at 4-0, Pocket dropped a 361 kitty, Saltese walked off the Survivor bus, and Wednesday's FAAB clear saw Drummond blow $42 on one linebacker. Last Ride this week is Morningside vs Saltese, and the loser is out for good.
method: W/L + win quality + roster ceiling + FAAB + pedigree + sit/start + trades; PF is evidence, not the ranking.

rankings.blurb: Juice: still the only unbeaten team in WU country. Reese's 40 and Watt's 33 pushed a 147-point defense past Ultron 280.5–225, Kittle added 25.5, and the PA (841.5) is still one of the league's lowest. Spent $11 on Amik Robertson (cut Camryn Bynum) and kept $70 in the holster. Junk: PF trails Pocket by 128 and Hyper by 19, so the 4-0 is partly good scheduling. Next up is the league's second-highest scoring offense, the team with the worst luck in the league.

Juice: 361. McMillan 51, CeeDee 47, Ernest Jones 45, a 192-point defense and the season-high kitty, Pocket's second. League-best PF by more than 100 and the fattest wallet ($111) after a pair of $0 fliers (Jonah Coleman, Jalen Pitre). Junk: Dalton Kincaid's 1.5, again. The Host is the best team on paper, and the only thing between him and No. 1 is Heff's zero in the loss column. A trip to 0-4 Drummond is a scrimmage.

Juice: Kyren 40, Puka 33, Stroud 32 and a 161-point offense beat Hyper 280–234.5. Jesse's LAB has quietly won three straight and the 843.5 PA is one of the lowest in the league. Sat out waivers with $67 in the bank. Junk: 950.5 PF is middle of the pack, and Demario Davis (31) is basically the whole defense. Morningside comes to town playing Last Ride with nothing to lose.

Juice: Rymo's SPD's survived Drummond 226.5–215 the WR way. Higgins 32, Flowers 31, JT 24, and Nathan Landman (21) is already paying off from the Saltese trade. At the clear they spent $16 on Kirk Cousins and $1 on Seth McGowan, and cut Courtland Sutton. Junk: won by 11.5 against a team whose three flex starters scored 3 total. SPD's are 3-1 with a PF that won't scare anyone, and Substation's 172-point defense is waiting.

Juice: two straight wins, and the defense keeps carrying. Evan Williams 36, Brooks 27, Mack Wilson 21 (a parting gift before the trade) and Warner 20 made a 131-point WU unit, and B-Rob (27) plus Bowers (25.5) did enough to edge the Slumlords 226–218.5. Then on Oct 6 the Eddies shipped Hampton and Mack Wilson to Saltese for Breece Hall and Rhamondre Stevenson, no FAAB involved, so the backfield just got a lot deeper. Spent $6 on Tuli Tuipulotu and $2 to bring Chimere Dike back (cut Kendre Miller), with $71 left. Junk: the offense managed 95, and Garrett Wilson's 5 was a big part of why. Leonard Williams is a DL nursing an ankle, so no help there. A 2-2 team with a top-five PF still has to prove it isn't a .500 team.

Juice: Tim's Divers won twice off one score. 223.5 beat Saltese and kept them alive on Last Ride over the Slumlords. C.J. Henderson 34, Ollie Gordon 25 and Isaiah Williams 23 led it. Picked up Aaron Rodgers for $0 at the clear (cut Gabe Jacas). Junk: 841.0 PF is the lowest in the league, and the 3-1 is lying for them. This week is Last Ride vs Saltese, and LAB on the road is a tough place to try and survive.

Juice: Nate's Week 4 waiver haul finally scored. Emmanwori 38, Izien 34 and Edmunds 34 made a 172-point defense, and Substation beat TTAB 295.5–216 to get back to .500. Junk: 879 PF is still bottom-four, and Substation sat out this week's waivers with $30 left. Rymo's SPD's are a real test of whether last week was the new normal or a one-off.

Juice: second-most points in the league, and Kenneth Walker III (39) took the OMVP lead at 142 YTD. Spent $11 on Jaylin Noel and dropped Bo Nix. Junk: Kenyon Sadiq went from 34.5 to 0, Egbuka added 3, and 1-3 with the league's second-highest PF is the most painful stat in WU country. They're ranked on the roster, not the record, and a road trip to the 4-0 Goats is a chance to make the record match.

Juice: 268.5 in a loss is fifth-best on the week. Nico Collins 36, Hubbard 33, Singleton 33. Kyle reloaded hard: Mason Graham $6 midweek, then Byron Young $4 (cut Dexter Lawrence), Tre Harris $4 (cut Dontayvion Wicks) and Keisean Nixon $0 (cut C. Gardner-Johnson), with $91 still in the bank. Junk: 1-3 with 1120.5 PA, and they just lost by 92.5. The two-time champ is running out of time to start winning.

Juice: Javonte Williams 33 and Emanuel Wilson 31 matched Substation on offense (123 to 123.5), and Jeremiah Trotter's 37 was a one-man defense. Chase rebuilt the front and back seven on Wednesday morning with three free-agent swaps: +Khalil Mack/−Bradley Chubb, +Mansoor Delane/−Treydan Stukes, +Dane Belton/−Andre Cisco. Junk: a 93-point defense lost by 79, Wingard and Cisco scored 2 each (Cisco is gone now), and Josh Allen managed 19. Two straight Ls since the Week 1 kitty.

Juice: Cooper 34 and Sherwood 32 kept the defense honest, Tate added 26, and Luke went all in at the clear: Dohnte Meyers $17, plus $1 each on Chase Young, Alontae Taylor and Cole Bishop, and Teddye Buchanan $0 (cut Jordan Battle). Junk: 206.5 was the league floor, JSN scored 12, Stafford 13, Montgomery 4, and that score got them kicked off the Survivor bus. Two straight Ls, $11 left, and Last Ride vs Morningside this week, where losing means out for good.

Juice: Maye bounced back from 1 to 30, Judkins and Budda Baker had 23 each, and Rousseau leads the DMVP race at 137. Ryan spent $30 on Will Shipley (cut Lukas Van Ness) and $7 to bring back Romeo Doubs (cut Dalton Schultz). Junk: two Ls off one score. 218.5 lost to Eagle Ridge by 7.5 and to Morningside on Last Ride by 5, so re-entry is finished. 1145 PA is the worst in the league.

Juice: Monangai 37, Bryce Young 31, Campbell 27 and Turner 26. There's a team in there. Junk: Saquon 1, Chase 5, Barham 2, and a 55.5-point loss to the Goats. Brian spent the last $1 on Jacoby Brissett (cut Sam Darnold) and added Mike Gesicki and Mark Andrews for $0, so the wallet is officially empty. Every fix from here comes off the bench.

Juice: Bijan 41, Burrow 35, Hamilton 26, Olave 25, Strange 22, and they still lost by 11.5. Gavin went big on Wednesday with $42 on Isaiah McDuffie, the biggest bid of the week, and has $3 left. Junk: McConkey 0, Parker Washington 1 and D.J. Moore 2 in starting slots, and 0-4. The Host and his 361 are up next.
